backward_compat_traps.rule: The 16-bit LID is unique only within a subnet; cross-subnet forwarding uses the 128-bit GID in the GRH.
backward_compat_traps.trap: Using a LID across subnets fails — routers forward on the GID, switches on the LID.

backward_compat_traps.rule: VL15 carries management (SMPs) and is never flow controlled.
backward_compat_traps.trap: Applying data-VL credit accounting to VL15 is wrong.
Treating credits as incremental breaks recovery after a lost Flow Control Packet.

backward_compat_traps.rule: RC/UC/UD/RD are per-QP; UD is single-MTU and connectionless.
backward_compat_traps.trap: Assuming RDMA on UD, or multi-MTU messages on UD, is invalid.

backward_compat_traps.rule: 8b/10b for SDR/DDR/QDR; 64b/66b for FDR and above; PAM4 for HDR/NDR.
backward_compat_traps.trap: Assuming 8b/10b at EDR/HDR (it is 64b/66b) miscomputes the effective data rate.

fields.spec_version: InfiniBand Architecture Specification (IBTA), Volume 1 Core Architecture + Volume 2 Physical, Release 1.x
previous_versions: InfiniBand 1.0 — initial IBTA release establishing the layered fabric (Channel Adapters, switches/routers, Subnet Manager, LRH/GRH/BTH, Queue Pairs, verbs, SDR).

key_changes.summary: Successive IBTA releases added DDR (5), QDR (10) on 8b/10b, then FDR (14), EDR (25), HDR (50), NDR (100) Gbps/lane on 64b/66b with PAM4 for HDR/NDR — the layered architecture (CAs, switches/routers, SM, LRH/GRH/BTH, Queue Pairs, verbs, RC/UC/UD/RD) is carried forward unchanged.

fields.version_naming_history_note: InfiniBand is maintained by the InfiniBand Trade Association (IBTA). The architecture is split into Volume 1 (Core Architecture) and Volume 2 (Physical). Link-speed generations are named SDR / DDR / QDR / FDR / EDR / HDR / NDR (2.5 / 5 / 10 / 14 / 25 / 50 / 100 Gbps per lane). Facts here are grounded in the IBTA InfiniBand Architecture Specification.
